the existence of employee stock options encourages companies to repurchase their shares.

“the desire to avoid the negative effects of stock option dilution on the value of the company is one of the motives that can lead to the repurchase of shares, and that directors holding a significant number of stock options are the ones who are most likely to encourage the company to make such repurchases”.

the development of employee stock options can explain the increase in share repurchases, that the desire to avoid the associated dilution is one of the reasons for making these repurchases, and that the existence of stock options held by directors can explain the existence of share repurchases.

the impact of stock options on the financing policy of companies.
the impact of stock option plans on the policies of share repurchases.
the impact of the existence of stock options on the policies of equity repurchase.

the existence of managerial options does not have any significant impact on the repurchase and dividend policies.

managers who are more inclined to use share repurchasing programs to avoid diluting their own options are also more inclined to reduce dividends to shareholders.

the existence of managerial options is a significant variable in the decision to make share repurchase programs.
